recent_posts.title: Unity AI Open Beta: AI Assistant
recent_posts.summary: Unity AI Assistant is now in open beta, integrated directly into the Unity 6 editor. It offers three modes: Ask (Q&A and guidance), Plan (turning ideas into structured implementation plans), and Agent (making direct changes to your project). Agent mode can automate tasks like placing objects in a scene, auditing game objects for polygon counts, generating scripts, creating 3D assets from images, and matching lighting styles. AI Gateway allows third-party coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor to be connected via API keys. Checkpoints save scene states before each AI change, enabling easy rollback. All AI-generated assets are tagged for easy identification and replacement later.

recent_posts.title: Analyze Profiler captures with Unity AI.
recent_posts.summary: Unity AI can now analyze profiler captures to automatically surface performance bottlenecks and suggest fixes, reducing the time developers spend manually digging through profiling data to optimize game performance.

recent_posts.title: Unity AI Open Beta: Introduction
recent_posts.summary: Unity 6 introduces an AI assistant and AI generators directly in the Unity editor. The AI assistant has three modes: Ask (read-only Q&A and project inspection), Plan (turning ideas into implementation plans), and Agent (automating repetitive tasks like auditing game objects and resolving errors). Unity MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets the editor act as a server for external AI clients, while the AI Gateway lets you connect third-party models like Claude, Gemini, Codex, and Cursor. AI Generators create placeholder assets for rapid prototyping. Installation is available via the Package Manager for Unity 6.0–6.2 or via the AI dropdown for 6.3+, and requires a Unity Cloud project connection.

CTV and mobile gaming: How brands are closing the second-screen gap
recent_posts.summary: Second-screen behavior during TV viewing is fragmenting advertiser attention, and brands are increasingly pairing Connected TV (CTV) campaigns with mobile gaming placements to recapture it. The post outlines three use cases: extending live sports sponsorships into gaming moments, reinforcing back-to-school campaigns by targeting parents during nighttime gaming sessions, and amplifying trailer bursts across both screens. The argument is that today's gaming audience is mainstream — parents, professionals, decision-makers — making mobile gaming a natural complement to CTV buys rather than a niche add-on. Unity positions its combined CTV and gaming solutions as the way to measure and act on cross-screen attention.

recent_posts.title: 2D Beginner Adventure: Robot Repair
recent_posts.summary: Robot Repair is a beginner-friendly Unity course for 2D game development, updated for Unity 6.3. It walks learners through building a complete 2D adventure game step-by-step, covering player movement, world building, hazards, collectibles, enemies, UI, game loops, dialogue, scripting, audio, and visual effects. The course offers multiple visual style asset packs for customization and includes a playable demo on Unity Play.

top_posts.title: An open letter to our community
top_posts.summary: Unity Personal plan will remain free and there will be no Runtime Fee for games built on Unity Personal. No game with less than $1 million in trailing 12-month revenue will be subject to the fee. For those creators on Unity Pro and Unity Enterprise, we are also making changes based on your feedback.

top_posts.title: Inside the Survival Kids Multiplayer Network Architecture
top_posts.summary: Unity Studio Productions developed Survival Kids as a day-one Nintendo Switch 2 launch title using Unity 6 and Netcode for Entities. The team created a unified network architecture supporting single-player, local co-op, online multiplayer, and GameShare functionality. They used Unity Relay for cloud hosting and maintained a single codebase for all play modes by treating single-player as a networked game with in-process connections. The biggest challenge was optimizing performance to run both server and client simulation simultaneously while maintaining 60 FPS.
